title: SDK function-calling safety layer and resumable streaming primitives
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a client-side safety layer for function (tool) invocation across our Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs plus ergonomics for resumable streaming responses. The goal is a consistent developer experience and reliable retry semantics when functions may be invoked from model-generated advice. This work complements runtime-side schema checks and is a pre-req for the Dedicated rollout because customer infra can expose side-effectful functions.
background:
Motivation:
- Recent customer incidents show model-led function calls may be retried by the platform and accidentally trigger side effects (duplicate downstream ops).
- SDKs currently validate schemas in different ways across languages, resulting in buggy coercions and inconsistent developer ergonomics.
- Streaming function outputs (partial JSON, multi-part attachments) are fragile: network blips cause full restarts and poor UX.
We need: (1) a lightweight, language-idiomatic safety layer that classifies calls as idempotent or not; (2) consistent schema validation/coercion modes (strict/permissive); (3) resumable stream primitives that allow the SDK to resume when the server supports it or gracefully fallback to restart when not supported.
design_decisions:
High-level decisions made so far:
- Validation modes: strict (reject non-exact matches), permissive (coerce missing numeric types, allow extra keys). Default: strict in production; permissive in dev via config flag.
- Idempotency tagging: SDK exposes .invoke({function, args, idempotencyKey?: string, sideEffect: boolean}) — platform tooling will use idempotencyKey to route/retry. SDK will reject retries for calls marked sideEffect=true unless the client supplies a non-replayable token.
- Retry policy: classify errors as transient (network, 5xx, crypto timeouts) vs permanent (schema mismatch, 4xx). SDK implements an exponential backoff with jitter for transient classes; a separate path for streamed invocations (see streaming section).
- Streaming resume token: server will optionally include a resumeToken in stream metadata. SDK will buffer last-acknowledged event position and attempt resume when transient error occurs. If resumeToken missing, SDK can either: (a) restart the function invocation (default for idempotent=true), or (b) surface a partial-result error to the caller when sideEffect=true.
- Cross-language parity: public surface should be conceptually identical in Python/TS/Go; idiomatic shims will be used to surface language-native async/await or channel patterns.
schema_validation_strategy:
- Shared JSON schema artifacts published to the model-onboarding repo; SDKs will vend a generated validator at build time (ts/py/go codegen).
- Runtime coercion layer (opt-in via permissive mode) that attempts simple transforms: strings->numbers, truncation for overlength strings (with warning).
- Failure modes: immediate exception in strict mode; ValidationError object with details in permissive mode. SDKs will include a one-line actionable suggestion (e.g., 'missing field "email": add or mark optional in function schema').
- Telemetry: emit validation.{pass|warn|fail} with schema_id and validator_version.
streaming_implementation_notes:
- Buffering & checkpoints: SDK will emit periodic checkpoints (event index, byte offset) so clients can persist progress.
- Resume token mechanics: resumeToken is opaque; when present server must accept resume requests including lastCheckpoint. Server may reply 410 (gone) if the underlying invocation context expired — SDK must surface RetryableResumeFailed for idempotent calls.
- Partial JSON assembly: for function outputs that assemble into a full JSON object (e.g., large list), SDK will expose 'partial' and 'final' events. Partial events are not validated against final schema until 'final' arrives, but a running lightweight schema check will ensure types are not wildly divergent (safety check).
- Backpressure: streaming API will accept a client-specified maxInflightChunks to avoid unbounded memory growth.
safety_and_retries:
- Side-effect guard: default is conservative: if function is declared sideEffect=true in schema, SDK will not automatically retry without explicit client token.
- Retryable errors include: transient network, 429/503 with Retry-After, server-side transient errors. Non-retryable: schema validation errors, auth errors, client misconfiguration.
- Retry windows: SDK will not exceed a configurable retry budget (default 30s for interactive calls, 2m for background tasks).
- Observability: emit span annotations: function.invoke.{start|retry|success|fail}, include idempotencyKey and validation outcome but never log PII.
compatibility_notes:
- We will ship shims that mirror existing method names but deprecate older patterns (e.g., .callFunction -> .invoke). Deprecations will be signaled via warnings for two minor releases.
- For older platform deployments that don't support resumeToken, SDK falls back to restart logic documented above.
testing_and_acceptance:
Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests for all three SDKs covering: strict validation reject, permissive coerce+warn, idempotent retry resume success with resumeToken, resume failure fallback when resumeToken absent.
- Unit tests for validator codegen: validators must produce deterministic error messages (stable strings).
- Integration benchmarks: median additional client CPU < 5% vs current SDK for small schemas; streaming memory bounded with checkpoints for >100k events.
- Docs: published SDK guide with code examples and an architecture note in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Function+Calling+Safety+Layer (preview).
- PR links: GH PRs will be created per language and must include interop tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls (placeholder).
implementation_plan:
MVP -> Iterations:
- MVP (this ticket): validation modes + idempotency flag + basic streaming resume support (resumeToken aware) in TS/Py/Go clients.
- Iteration 1: codegen improvements, telemetry enrichment, default to strict for production.
- Iteration 2: UX additions: sandbox mode that simulates resume failures for testing; helper CLI to generate resume tokens for local e2e testing.
- Rollout: feature gate in console; enable for 10% of hosted users then 100% after telemetry stable.

open_questions: Should SDK expose a user-visible resumeToken API surface or keep tokens internal and rely on persisted checkpoints?
What's the best default for permissive mode in serverless environments where silent coercion is surprising?
Do we require platform to sign resumeTokens (HMAC) to prevent spoofing or accept opaque tokens?
risks:
- Potential for duplicate side effects if clients mis-mark functions as idempotent.
- Complexity of cross-lang codegen and keeping validator versions in sync.
- Resume semantics rely on server cooperation; partial adoption will complicate UX.
